summary: P0 per owner: NV01_ROOT_NON_PRIV host client + per-birth privileged tripwire, re-measured as root on the box; P1/P2 per owner: identity windows out of passthrough spaces, Translated in its own VAS; adversarial reviews

nonpriv.ci: Green on all three pushes. dc64b22b ran in GitHub Actions run 37148530702, 55743ecd in 37148789381, and 51308a20 (the head) in 37150145697. In each run the 'stable' job (build, test, clippy, fmt and the boundary/unsafe gates) and the 'aarch64' job passed. The 'slow' job was skipped, as it is on push. Before each commit I ran: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check (OK), debt.py claims (new=0) and check_sections.sh (0 offenders). The unsafe ratchet for kf-linux-raw moved from 75 to 77 and is itemised in ci.yml.
nonpriv.before: QEMU runs as root on the bench, so every host channel kf3 created was an ADMIN channel. Box 54050499 (RTX 3060, 580.159.04 open module), branch v3-sec-p0 at rev 3e0f6dee, probe arm: 6 channel births, each reply flags 0x004000a0, PRIVILEGED_CHANNEL=1. The dispatched fix was to allocate the root client as NV01_ROOT_NON_PRIV, and it cannot work on Linux. ogkm-580 escape.c:394-403 rewrites every userspace root allocation to NV01_ROOT_CLIENT, so bIsRootNonPriv (client.c:88) is never set. I measured this as root on the box. Root clients requested as NV01_ROOT, NV01_ROOT_NON_PRIV and NV01_ROOT_CLIENT all came back as class 0x41 and admin (NV0000 GET_PRIVILEGED_STATUS returned 0x5). The admin decision is capable(CAP_SYS_ADMIN) of the calling thread, made on every ioctl (escape.c:304, nv-linux.h:537). With CAP_SYS_ADMIN cleared from the thread's effective set, every client reported 0x0, including clients created as admin. Restoring the bit brought back 0x5.
nonpriv.after: The 'bit' the owner meant is CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the effective capability set of the thread that creates the channel. kf3 now clears that bit only for the one channel-create call, then restores it. QEMU still runs as root and the bench is unchanged; kf3 does not refuse to run with CAP_SYS_ADMIN. Every channel reply is checked. If RM marks the channel privileged, or its privilege level is not USER, the channel is refused by name and freed. All results below are on box 54050499 with QEMU as root (uid 0, CapEff 000001ffffffffff). Same probe arm at dc64b22b: the same 6 births, every reply 0x00000080 PRIVILEGED_CHANNEL=0 privilege=USER, FAST_VERDICT=PASS. Negative control (KF3_NEGCTL_SKIP_CAP_BRACKET=1, which skips the clearing): the first reply was 0x000000a0, the check refused it by name and freed the channel, and the run failed as it should. Merge bar at 55743ecd: EXIT rc=0; kf-* tests 1764 passed, 0 failed; v3 gates 9/9; bare-metal suite 30/30; 30-arm thin-guest suite 30/30. All 161 channel births in the suite and all 11 in the gates read PRIVILEGED_CHANNEL=0, and none was refused. Mutation check: disabling the reply check, or the bit clearing, turns a unit test red.
fixed: New module crates/kf-linux-raw/src/capability.rs, backed by capability_unsafe.rs (capget and capset on the calling thread). with_effective_cap_cleared(cap, call) clears one capability from the calling thread's effective set for one call, then restores it. The permitted set is untouched, so the VMM's privileges are unchanged.

crates/kf-host/src/channel.rs: birth_member makes the channel-create ioctl with CAP_SYS_ADMIN cleared this way. If the bit cannot be cleared, the birth is refused before any host call (CAP_BRACKET_REFUSED 0x4B74).

The reply check is birth_privilege(). It refuses by name and frees the channel (PRIVILEGED_CHANNEL_REFUSED 0x4B73) when NVOS04_FLAGS_PRIVILEGED_CHANNEL (bit 5) is set, when the reply's internalFlags privilege is not USER, when the reply is too short to read, or when the request itself asked for bit 5. The request is built by channel_alloc_request() and never asks for bit 5. Every birth logs one line with the reply flags.

Six unit tests in kf-host and four in kf-linux-raw that fail without the change. They cover: the request never asks for bit 5; a privileged reply (including the BEFORE value 0x004000a0) is refused; a non-USER internal level is refused; unreadable replies and privileged requests are refused; the bit clearing restores the thread's sets exactly and never touches another thread.

Step 1 check (nothing kf3 needs is admin-only). I read these ogkm-580 sources: escape.c:394-403 (the class rewrite); client.c:88 and :384-394 (rmclientIsAdmin); kernel_channel.c:277-291 (where privilege is stamped); and kernel_channel.c:1056-1058 (RM zeroes internalFlags before copying the reply back, so bit 5 is the only reading that carries the verdict on 580). Only the channel-create call runs without the bit. The privilege checks reachable from that call need KERNEL, not admin: kernel_channel_group_api.c:310, usermode_api.c:72 and kernel_channel.c:4271. Admin checks that use the client's cached privilege are unaffected by the change: mapping_cpu.c:668 (CPU map of REGMEM) and kernel_graphics_manager.c:465 (MIG routing). An ADMIN GR channel gets the unrestricted privileged-register access map (kernel_graphics_context.c:3293-3297); that is now avoided. The suite passing confirms kf3 needs nothing admin-only at channel creation.

THE_CONSTRAINTS.md §30: the privilege rule is folded in above the w748 correction. It quotes the owner. It states that the mechanism is the calling thread's effective CAP_SYS_ADMIN at the channel-create call, the reply check is the tripwire, and the client class is not a mechanism.

Evidence is in traces/v3_security/nonpriv_20261003/: a README with defensive wording, the probe script and its log, the BEFORE logs copied from the v3-sec-p0 worktree, the AFTER and negative-control logs, and merge_bar/ with its own README.

open: Owner decision needed: the mechanism is not the one dispatched. The task named NV01_ROOT_NON_PRIV as the mechanism; on Linux it does nothing (escape.c rewrites it, measured on the box). What was built instead clears the effective CAP_SYS_ADMIN bit for the channel-create call only. This is the owner's 'clearing a bit' in its literal sense, it does not refuse to run as root, and it does not change how QEMU runs. The client allocation was left as NV01_ROOT_CLIENT, with a comment explaining why. This is a security-policy change, so the owner reviews it before merge (§F). Nothing was pushed to master or v3.

Not covered: libcuda's own channels. The walker (C2) and display (C3) libcuda contexts still create channels under the VMM's capabilities, so they are ADMIN when QEMU is root. They run only kayfabe-authored kernels; no guest pushbuffer reaches them. Applying the same clearing around their context creation is possible but was not done.

Not addressed by this task: the other points in the owner's message. (a) The identity windows (the whole store and all guest RAM) are mapped into every twin VA space, including user ones. Passthrough does not need them. (b) Translated rings live in the guest kernel's twin VA space; the owner wants a separate space holding at most the single-store guest VRAM. Both remain open.

Repository process: OWNER_RULINGS.md has no entry for the owner's 2026-10-03 direction ('do not refuse CAP_SYS_ADMIN if clearing a bit fixes it; sandboxing the VMM is not our job'). It is quoted only in THE_CONSTRAINTS §30.
Box state: /root/kayfabe on box 54050499 is left detached at 55743ecd. The kf3 binaries for dc64b22b and 55743ecd are under /workspace/bench/kf3-bins/.

findings: MECHANISM IS SOUND (verified against ogkm-580 source). escape.c:394-403 rewrites NV01_ROOT, NV01_ROOT_NON_PRIV and NV01_ROOT_CLIENT to NV01_ROOT_CLIENT, so client.c:88 bIsRootNonPriv is never set from userspace. escape.c:304 sets the privilege level per call from osIsAdministrator(), which is capable(CAP_SYS_ADMIN) (nv-linux.h:537). kernel_channel.c:277-291 stamps the channel from that per-call level, and in the USER branch RM leaves the flags alone, so the readback is exact as long as the request never sets bit 5. kernel_channel.c:1056-1058 zeroes internalFlags before copy-out, so bit 5 is the reading that carries the verdict. kgrctxGetRegisterAccessMapId (kernel_graphics_context.c:3293) keys on the channel's privilegeLevel (kchannelCheckIsAdmin, kernel_channel.c:2148-2155), so bracketing the channel-create call does remove the unrestricted priv-access map. privprobe.py and its log match this: the client class has no effect, and clearing CAP_SYS_ADMIN from the calling thread's effective set flips 0x5 to 0x0 per call, even on clients born as admin.

ROOT-CLIENT CHECK, which cannot be met as worded: kf3 has exactly one RM root client (kf-host/src/lib.rs:284 OwnClient::allocate_root, opened once from kf-qemu/src/device.rs:233; the kf-gate binaries open their own). On Linux it cannot be NON_PRIV, as shown above. I checked that the channel is the only guest-steered object whose properties depend on the creator's privilege. Every host control kf3 issues is RMCTRL_FLAGS_NON_PRIVILEGED (0x8 bit) in the 580 nvoc tables: 0x20801210, 0x20801208, 0xa06c0101/0102/0103/0105, 0x00801909, 0x2080130e, 0x20802a03, 0x20802502, 0x83de0309, 0xc36f0108, 0xa06f0103, 0x3d05, 0x3d06. Every class kf3 allocates is non-privileged; NV01_MEMORY_LOCAL_PHYSICAL is privileged and is not used, the store is NV01_MEMORY_LOCAL_USER. The per-call privilege gates in the VA-space, memory, os-descriptor, TSG and usermode paths require KERNEL, not admin. The remaining client-cached-admin effects (REGMEM CPU map at mapping_cpu.c:667, MIG routing) have no guest-steered caller. So the builder's substitute, a per-call clear at the channel create plus a reply check, covers what NON_PRIV was meant to cover.

EVIDENCE CHECKS OUT. after_root_run.log: launcher euid=0, QEMU pid 89538 'Uid: 0 0 0 0 CapPrm/CapEff 000001ffffffffff', binary dc64b22b. All 6 births read reply_flags=0x00000080 PRIVILEGED_CHANNEL=0 privilege=USER cap_sys_admin=cleared-for-call; that last field can only print when the thread held CAP_SYS_ADMIN, so the run itself shows it was privileged. The negative control (also QEMU uid 0, full CapEff) got a live 0x000000a0 reply, refused it by name and freed the channel, and the run then failed. The BEFORE logs are byte-identical to /workspace/kf-sec-p0/traces/v3_security/p0_20261003/measure_root_*. Merge bar: 161/161 suite births and 11/11 gate births are PRIVILEGED_CHANNEL=0 with cleared-for-call; tests 1764/0, gates 9/9, bare 30/30, fast 30/30. dc64b22b to 55743ecd and 55743ecd to 51308a20 change no code; the later commits touch docs and traces only, and there are no binaries. CI runs 37148530702, 37148789381 and 37150145697 are green (stable and aarch64 jobs), and the new tests appear in the CI log. Re-run locally: debt.py claims new=0, check_sections offenders=0, rustfmt --check clean. The branch merges cleanly onto origin/master (12a526df).

TESTS CAN FAIL ONLY PARTLY, and the builder's 'Mutating either check turns a test red' is overstated. I verified this with mutants in a scratch copy. (1) Deleting the clearing capset inside with_effective_cap_cleared turns the_bracket_clears_effective_for_the_call_and_restores_it red when run as root. The same test binary run unprivileged (setpriv to uid 65534, CapEff=0, the same as GitHub's runner user) stays 4/4 GREEN, because the test takes the NotHeld path. CI therefore cannot catch a broken bracket; only the root merge bar on the box can. (2) Changing birth_member (kf-host/src/channel.rs:778-825) so the bracket never runs and the birth_privilege match is replaced by Ok: all kf-host and kf-linux-raw tests stay green, even as root. Nothing tests the wiring. merge_check.sh does not gate on the birth lines either; the 161/161 count was a manual grep. With both removed, the box suite would also pass silently, just as BEFORE passed with privileged channels. Fix: (a) add a gate in the style of own_client_invariant.rs, or a seam test, that goes red if the channel-class allocation in birth_member is not inside with_effective_cap_cleared and followed by birth_privilege; (b) make merge_check/gates fail if any 'channel birth' line lacks PRIVILEGED_CHANNEL=0, or if there are no birth lines; (c) run the live capability test under sudo in CI, or state in the test that it is vacuous for non-root runs.

THE TRIPWIRE COVERS EVERY BIRTH PATH TODAY, BUT NOTHING ENFORCES IT. Every channel-class allocation goes through HostRm::birth_member: directly from kf-chan/src/passthrough.rs:123, and through birth_channel from passthrough.rs:126, kf-chan/src/host.rs:206 and kf-harness. However HostRm::raw_alloc (kf-host/src/lib.rs:810) is pub and accepts any class, including the gpfifo channel class; kf-qemu/src/rmfacts.rs:63 already calls it directly from another crate. A future channel allocation at any raw_alloc call site would skip both the bracket and the reply check. Suggest moving the check to where the bound lives: in carried_alloc/raw_alloc, refuse the channel class unless it comes from the bracketed birth path, or apply the bracket and reply check whenever the class is the family's gpfifo channel class.

DOC GOING STALE ON MERGE: origin/master's docs/design/V3_SECURITY_AUDIT_PLAN.md (commit 12a526df, not on this branch) says at line 36 and line 168 that the fix on v3-sec-nonpriv is 'NV01_ROOT_NON_PRIV + a per-birth tripwire'. That is the mechanism this branch measured as a no-op. The merge is textually clean, so the wrong claim would survive. Under the repo's own doc-hygiene rule (record the supersession in the superseded text), the branch should merge or rebase master and correct both lines to 'per-call CAP_SYS_ADMIN clear + reply check; NON_PRIV is rewritten by escape.c:394-403'. Note also that master's OWNER_RULINGS §P now quotes 'Sandboxing vmm is not our job', so the builder's open item that OWNER_RULINGS has no entry is half out of date. The other half of the owner's direction, do not refuse CAP_SYS_ADMIN if clearing a bit fixes it, is still recorded only in THE_CONSTRAINTS §30.

MINOR ACCURACY: (a) kf-host/src/lib.rs, in the doc for PRIVILEGED_CHANNEL_REFUSED, cites 'OWNER_RULINGS §N' for the rule that every host channel must be USER. §N is the X11 GF100_DISP_SW ruling. It mentions the single store but not channel privilege; cite THE_CONSTRAINTS §30 and OWNER_RULINGS §P instead. (b) The capability.rs module doc and the dc64b22b commit message say 'two capget/capset pairs'; the code makes one capget and two capsets. (c) The AFTER run's arm list is '--probe-launch-dma,--probe-launch-dma' (passed twice) while BEFORE ran it once. The births match (6 each), so this does not matter, but the README's 'same arm' wording hides it.

RESIDUAL, DISCLOSED, NOT BLOCKING: the libcuda contexts (walker C2 at kf-cuda/src/walk.rs:776 and display C3 at kf-cuda/src/display.rs:183) still create ADMIN channels when QEMU is root. libcuda authors those pushbuffers and no guest pushbuffer reaches them, so this is defense in depth only. This contradicts master's audit-plan line 36 ('must not make its host channels privileged'). For the follow-up: bracketing only cuCtxCreate would miss channels libcuda creates lazily later. It would be more robust to run each libcuda worker thread with CAP_SYS_ADMIN cleared from its effective set for the thread's whole life, before cuInit, so that libcuda's internal threads inherit the cleared set. The owner's other two points (identity windows in user twin VA spaces, and Translated rings in the guest-kernel twin space) are untouched, as the builder reported.

FAIL-CLOSED EDGE, no change needed: if capset is denied while CAP_SYS_ADMIN is in the effective set (for example an SELinux-confined root QEMU without the process:setcap permission), every birth is refused with CAP_BRACKET_REFUSED 0x4B74. This is consistent with 'a channel RM stamps otherwise never runs' and is documented. QEMU 10.2.4's own seccomp policy does not block capget/capset (system/qemu-seccomp.c). A panic inside the bracket, or a failed restore, leaves the thread without CAP_SYS_ADMIN in effect, which is the direction that cannot widen anything. Docs: the README and THE_CONSTRAINTS text are defensive, describing properties and checks without attack procedure. I made no edits to the branch or worktree. The mutants were built in a scratch git-archive copy with a separate CARGO_TARGET_DIR, and the copy and the target dir were deleted afterwards.

p1p2.summary:
This is a read-only design for P1 and P2. Nothing was edited and no box was run. kf-master code was read at origin/master 7c9234d2, whose crates/kf-* are identical to the worktree head 784465a1. RM and UVM behaviour comes from ogkm-580.

**What is true today.** Translated work does NOT run in the walker's or the display's CUDA contexts (C2/C3). It runs in C1's host mirror of the guest kernel's own VA space (chan.rs:2945-2947). Every mirror, user mirrors included, also carries both identity windows (mem.rs:1755-1762) and a ring region. That placement was a convenience from §12. A UVM space is only known to be kernel at its first Translated birth, which comes after its mirror and its spare were built. Putting the windows in every mirror guaranteed that a Translated birth found them. Passthrough work never uses the windows. Translated rewrites are their only consumer.

**The owner is right on both points.** The windows in user twins are the in-guest isolation hole (rule A.9). They also cost one guest-RAM window map per mirror: 65-86 ms measured, inside held replies.

**Proposal.** One Translated host VA space per VM (the T-space). It holds the store window, the guest-RAM window and kayfabe's rings, and nothing else:
- The pushbuffer and GPFIFO are mapped read-only, the fence read-write, and USERD is not mapped.
- Guest twins hold only guest rows: no windows, no rings, nothing kayfabe owns.
- The rewriter on Translated channels becomes an address re-author. Every address the engine dereferences is computed by kayfabe and lies inside a window:
  - physical operands keep today's arithmetic;
  - virtual operands, CE and host semaphore addresses are rewritten through the guest space's placement rows;
  - address registers the guest writes are never forwarded;
  - unknown methods are refused by name, and binding happens at submit, after any MEM_OP split.

**Why virtual operands must be rewritten, not refused.** Refusing them would break both stock producers:
- CeUtils' completions are virtual: a CE release at pbGpuVA+finishPayloadOffset and a host SEMAPHOREA-D release (channel_utils.c:671-673, 731-746).
- UVM's PTE/PDE writes copy from inline pushbuffer data at a virtual source (uvm_mmu.c:429-436, uvm_pte_batch.c:52-62). Its tracking releases and cross-channel acquires are virtual too.
- Their data operands are physical on every family we support (uvm_gpu.h:1679-1692, uvm_mmu.c:2330-2342; CeUtils VIRTUAL_MODE is off because kf serves raw comptag mode).

**Consequences.**
- UVM's USER→KERNEL flip no longer needs windows or a migration. It only decides whether privileged leaves are mirrored for resolution.
- Mixing user and kernel channels in one space becomes harmless.
- The ring/guest-VA collision and the `reserved()` refusals disappear.
- Completions stay native, because the engine still writes the guest's memory through the window alias.
- Mirror creation drops two window maps. The RAM window is built once per VM, at prewarm.

**Guest RAM in the T-space.** The RAM window has to stay, because UVM and CeUtils sysmem operands are guest-physical and mapping per operand would cost hundreds of host map calls per 2 MiB migration. That departs from the owner's literal "at most the store", so it goes to the owner.

**Found on the way.** Today's rewriter forwards three things verbatim that the allowlist closes:
- host CLEAR_FAULTED (0x84), carrying a guest-chosen opaque channel handle (UVM pushes it only on Turing, when servicing a non-replayable fault);
- CE SET_MONITORED_FENCE_SIGNAL_ADDR_*;
- CE SET_RENDER_ENABLE_A/B.

**P0 note.** NV01_ROOT_NON_PRIV cannot be the bit to clear. escape.c:394-403 forces every userspace root class to NV01_ROOT_CLIENT, so bIsRootNonPriv is never set from kf3. The bit that decides is CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the effective set of the thread issuing the channel alloc (escape.c:304, client.c:393). Dropping it on the birth threads, plus the bit-5 assert, needs no refusal. T channels carry no privileged operation either way.
p1p2.design_markdown:
# P1 + P2 — identity windows only where Translated work runs; Translated work in its own host VA space

Read at kf-master `origin/master` `7c9234d2` (crates identical to `784465a1`), ogkm-580.159.04. Read-only design; nothing run.

## 0. Short answer to the owner

**Why the windows are in every twin today.** `THE_TRANSLATED_PLANE.md` §12 (2026-09-21/22) decided it this way: *"Put the identity window in a Translated-only VAS — UVM mixes apertures in one stream ⇒ it goes in every host VAS"*. It is implemented at `kf-qemu/src/mem.rs:1755-1762`. The reasoning ran like this:
- Translated work ran verbatim in a host mirror of the guest kernel's own space (§24.2).
- UVM's space starts USER and only becomes kernel at its first Translated birth (`chan.rs:2900-2913`).
- That birth comes after the mirror and its prewarmed spare were built.
- Putting both windows into every mirror guaranteed the rewriter found them.

**You are right.**
- **Passthrough never uses the windows.** Only Translated rewrites emit window VAs.
- **Guest-kernel channels cannot be created from guest userspace.** `kernel_channel` needs an RM-internal client or `PRIVILEGE=KERNEL`, `kf-rm/src/chanlink.rs:1362-1382`.
- **The hole is the reverse direction.** Every user process's own passthrough channels run in a twin that maps the whole store and all guest RAM (rule A.9).
- **It also costs time on a held reply.** Each mirror pays a RAM-window map: 65-86 ms measured, inside a held page-directory reply (`mem.rs:947-952`).

**Where Translated runs today.** In C1's mirror of the guest kernel space (`chan.rs:2945-2947`), never in the walker's or the display's CUDA contexts (C2/C3). That mirror holds:
- guest rows;
- both windows;
- the 1 MiB kayfabe ring objects, which contain the pushbuffer, GPFIFO, fence and **USERD** (`kf-chan/src/host.rs:29-33`, `:145-156`).

Guest virtual operands and semaphores are forwarded unchanged (`kf-chan/src/translated.rs:26`).

**Proposal.** One **T-space** per VM: a host VA space that holds only:
- the store window;
- the guest-RAM window;
- kayfabe's rings, with pushbuffer and GPFIFO **read-only**, the fence read-write, and USERD **not mapped**.

No guest VA exists in it. Every address a Translated channel's engine dereferences is computed by kayfabe. Guest twins hold guest rows only, and the windows leave them.

## 1. What CeUtils and UVM actually push (why "refuse virtual operands" is not an option)

| producer | operand | aperture | size | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CeUtils memset/memcopy data | src/dst | **physical** unless `VIRTUAL_MODE` | up to the scrub chunk | `channel_utils.c:1036-1100` |
| CeUtils `VIRTUAL_MODE` | fbAlias src/dst | virtual, contiguous alias | large | Set only if `memmgrUseVasForCeMemoryOps`: SR-IOV-heavy, APM, or one-to-one comptag (`mem_scrub.c:152-155`, `mem_mgr_ga100.c:140-145`, `mem_mgr_gm107.c:1490-1494`). kf serves `Raw` comptag (`kf-rm/src/hostquery.rs:703`), so it is off. |
| CeUtils completion | CE `SET_SEMAPHORE_A/B` at `pbGpuVA+finishPayloadOffset` | **virtual** | 4 B | `channel_utils.c:671-673`, `:838-840` |
| CeUtils PB-get index | host `SEMAPHOREA-D` release at `pbGpuVA+semaOffset` | **virtual**, host method (40-bit) | 4 B | `channel_utils.c:731-746` |
| UVM migrations, memsets, PTE destinations | src/dst | **physical** on Turing…Blackwell non-SR-IOV and non-coherent Hopper | 4 KiB-2 MiB | `uvm_gpu.h:1679-1692`, `uvm_mmu.c:2330-2342`, `ce_phys_vidmem_write_supported=true` in `uvm_{volta,ampere,ada,blackwell}.c`, `uvm_hopper.c:75` |
| UVM PDE/PTE writes | CE memcopy **src = inline pushbuffer data** | **virtual** (UVM pushbuffer VA) | up to a PTE batch; may cross a 4 KiB page | `uvm_mmu.c:429-436`, `uvm_pte_batch.c:52-62`, `uvm_push.c:419-446` |
| UVM end-of-push tracking release | CE semaphore (reduction) | **virtual** | 4 B | `uvm_channel.c:1053-1063`, `:1512-1513` |
| UVM cross-channel dependency | host `SEM_ADDR_LO/HI` + `SEM_EXECUTE ACQ_CIRC_GEQ` | **virtual**, host (40-bit on Turing–Ada) | 4 B | `uvm_push.c:95-96`, `uvm_turing_host.c:53-70`; semaphores are kept below `max_host_va` (`uvm_gpu_semaphore.c:156`) |
| UVM tools read/write (cuda-gdb) | `uvm_mem` staging, kernel VA | virtual | ≤ page | `uvm_va_block.c:13065`, `:13172` |
| UVM pushbuffer itself | read by kf, not by the engine | sysmem by default | — | `uvm_pushbuffer.c:98-117` |

⇒ **Refusing virtual operands on Translated channels breaks both producers.** CeUtils loses its completions and `RmInitAdapter` times out. UVM loses every page-table write, so `cuInit` fails.

Two things make rewriting cheap:
- The data operands are physical, so today's arithmetic already covers them.
- The virtual operands are small: semaphores (naturally aligned, 4/8/16 bytes), inline data, and staging buffers.

## 2. The T-space

**Contents.** One `FERMI_VASPACE_A` per kf3 device, built in `prewarm` on the VA thread before the guest runs, from objects kayfabe owns. It is allocated **without** the guest VA reservations (`GUEST_VA_RANGES`, `kf-host/src/channel.rs:94-95`), because no guest row ever lands in it. It holds:
- **Store window.** `map_window(high=false)` lets RM place it bottom-up. §15/§17 measured `0x120000000` (4.5 GiB). The base is read back.
- **Guest-RAM window.** The same guest-RAM OS-descriptor object (with `CACHE_SNOOP`, §6), placed first-fit after the store window. §17 measured `0x405200000`.
- **Ring region** `[RING_REGION_BASE, 2^40)`, with rings mapped FIXED as today.

The build refuses by name if `ram_base + ram_len > RING_REGION_BASE`, which would mean a VM with about 1 TiB of RAM.

**Why the windows sit low.** Below 2^40 matters because host semaphore addresses are 40-bit on Turing–Ada (`SEMAPHOREA` 39:32, `SEM_ADDR_HI` 7:0). The rewritten CeUtils and UVM host semaphores must stay expressible. CE operands are 49-bit (57-bit from `C8B5`), so CE is unconstrained.

**One per VM, not one per kernel space.**
- There is no build at the UVM flip and no "migrate at flip" (the check's correction 4).
- The cost is paid once, before the guest runs. It is about what today's single prewarmed spare costs: RAM window 299 ms for 8 GiB including pinning, §16.2.
- Sharing is safe because no address the guest supplies reaches the engine unchanged.

**Rings.** Each Translated ring is born in the T-space. `HostRing::on_engine_at(rm, tspace.space, …)` is used with T-space ring slots instead of `mirror.rings`. Each ring maps three `SharedSlice` sub-ranges of its 1 MiB object at `ring_va + same offset`, so `va + GPFIFO_OFF` still holds:

| range | offsets | mapping |
|---|---|---|
| pushbuffer | `[0, 0xE_0000)` | read-only |
| GPFIFO | `[0xF_0000, +4 KiB)` | read-only |
| fence | `[0xF_8000, +4 KiB)` | read-write |
| USERD | `0xF_C000` | **not mapped** |

PBDMA reaches USERD through the instance block (`RingSpec{userd_memory, userd_offset}`), and kayfabe writes `GP_PUT` through its BAR1 CPU view, so both are unchanged. In the T-space the read-only mapping is defence in depth: no rewritten address can land in the ring region, because translation only yields window addresses bounded by window length. The cost is two extra map and unmap ioctls per Translated birth.

**Client.** Build it in C1 now, behind a `TSpace` struct that takes any `&HostRm`. OWNER_RULINGS §N already rules that kayfabe's own allocations leave the guest client. When the G/K split lands, the T-space and its rings move to K with two same-process dups (store and RAM object). The source allows this (`sharing.c:345-352`, `standard_mem.c:217-220`, `os_desc_mem.c:275-282`). T channels carry no host-RM VA lookups: `err_notifier 0`, no display-SW object, no debugger. So the VAS boundary is what enforces isolation here, and the client move is §N hygiene, not a precondition.

## 3. The rewriter in T-mode — the invariant and how it is enforced

**Invariant (new THE_CONSTRAINTS entry).**
- On a T-space channel, every address the engine dereferences is computed by kayfabe and lies inside the store window or the RAM window.
- A guest-written address value is never emitted.
- A method the class headers do not classify is refused by name.

**Address registers become state, never output.** These guest writes are held in `CeState` and not emitted:
- CE: `OFFSET_IN/OUT_UPPER/LOWER`, `SET_SEMAPHORE_A/B`;
- host: `SEMAPHOREA/B`, `SEM_ADDR_LO/HI`.

At each trigger the rewriter emits the translated values immediately before the trigger. The triggers are CE `LAUNCH_DMA`, host `SEMAPHORED`, and host `SEM_EXECUTE`, for release and acquire alike. This replaces today's "restore the guest's offsets after the launch" logic.

**Translation.**
- **Physical operand.** Unchanged arithmetic (`SlotWindow::translate`, `chan.rs:513-524`).
- **Virtual operand or semaphore.** Resolved through the placement rows of the guest VA space the channel was born in (`PlacedRows`, `mem.rs:458-487`). These are kayfabe's own placements, so this stays inside §56 rule 2 as P6b ruling (a) already reads it. Adjacent rows that are contiguous in both VA and backing are merged, and each piece maps to `fb_base+off` or `ram_base+off`.
- **Extents.**
  - Data operands use `extents()` (`translated.rs:676-720`).
  - Semaphores use 4, 8 or 16 bytes, by type, payload size and timestamp.
- **Permissions.** Rows record the guest leaf's `MapPerm`. A write (destination, release, reduction) through a read-only row is refused by name, as is a reduction through an `atomic_disable` row. Without that check the read-write window would silently widen the guest kernel's own read-only mappings.
- **Discontiguous operands.**
  - A **1-D** operand that spans discontiguous backing is split into pieces at the union of source and destination boundaries. A boundary that falls inside a remap element is refused.
  - Semaphore, interrupt and flush go only on the **last** piece, and that piece is `NON_PIPELINED`, so the release cannot precede the earlier pieces.
  - A multi-line operand must be contiguous over its whole pitch footprint, or it is refused.
  - A **block-linear virtual** operand is refused, because `extents` ignores layout.
- **Host semaphores.** A host-semaphore translation at or above `max_host_va` (2^40 on Turing–Ada) is refused by name.

**Bind at submit, not at fetch.** `ring.rs:216` rewrites a whole segment when it is fetched. A virtual operand that follows a `MEM_OP` split in the same segment would then be resolved against the rows from **before** the split's walk. That is the exact case of UVM writing PTEs, invalidating, and then using the new mapping.

So the rewriter emits a small IR: `Raw(words)`, `CeLaunch{regs,launch}`, `HostSem{regs,exec}`, `Invalidate{pdb}`. The pump binds each piece when it pushes to the host ring, after any earlier split completed. Physical operands could still bind early. Binding after the guest's last invalidate is legal TLB behaviour.

**Allowlists generated from the class headers** (`kf_chip::hwref`), for every CE class (C3B5…CAB5) and host class (C46F…CA6F):
- **Address methods:** rewritten as above.
- **Address-free state:** forwarded. This covers `LINE_LENGTH_IN`, `LINE_COUNT`, `PITCH_*`, `SET_REMAP_*`, `SET_SEMAPHORE_PAYLOAD(_UPPER)`, `NOP`, `WFI`, `YIELD`, `SET_REFERENCE`, `NON_STALL_INTERRUPT`, `MEM_OP` MEMBAR/L2, and `SET_OBJECT` of a CE class.
- **Everything else is refused by name**, including:
  - `SET_MONITORED_FENCE_SIGNAL_ADDR_*` (0x220/0x224) and `SET_RENDER_ENABLE_A/B` (0x254/0x258). Both are addresses, and both are forwarded verbatim today.
  - Hopper CC `SET_*ENCRYPT*/DECRYPT*` addresses.
  - **host `CLEAR_FAULTED` (0x84)**, which carries an RM-opaque channel handle (`clc56f.h:256-262`) and is forwarded verbatim today. UVM pushes it only on Turing, after servicing a non-replayable fault (`uvm_gpu_non_replayable_faults.c:290`). kayfabe does not deliver those faults yet, so refusing it costs nothing now. Whether GSP checks the handle against the issuing TSG is unverified (closed source).

`LAUNCH_DMA` fields are allowlisted the same way. `VPRMODE` must be 0 on C7B5, `COPY_TYPE` must be DEFAULT on C8B5 and later, and the fast scrub is converted as today.

`MEM_OP` TLB invalidate stays a split, and `GP100_UVM_SW` stays consumed. So no privileged operation ever reaches a T channel: no physical mode, no TLB invalidate, no ACCESS_COUNTER_CLR. That holds whatever the channel's privilege bit says.

## 4. Guest spaces after the change

- `create_mirror` and spares carry **no windows and no rings**. `reserved()` and `vmm_ranges()` become empty for twins, because no kayfabe placement exists in any space where guest-authored work runs. The ring-versus-guest-VA collision (§24.2, §25) is gone.
- **The UVM flip** (`chan.rs:2909`) changes no host mapping. It only lets the twin mirror privileged leaves, so the Translated resolver can resolve them. Measured at `5fead67d`: no privileged leaf was ever walked in a space that flipped this way.
- **Mixing rules, written so stock drivers never hit a refusal:**
  - A Translated birth in a space with a live passthrough channel is **allowed**, but the space stays USER and keeps withholding privileged leaves. A Translated operand that only a withheld leaf could resolve is refused by name.
  - A passthrough birth in a space whose twin has already mirrored a privileged leaf is refused by name.
  - Both cases are counted, and the expected count on the matrix is 0.
- **Spares** become plain spaces, so prewarm cost drops to near zero. The guest-RAM object is still created once (user twins map sysmem rows through it), and its pinning cost moves to the T-space build.

## 5. Completions

- **Native, unchanged in kind.** The engine writes the guest's semaphore itself, through the window alias of the same backing.
  - `Completion::for_route(Translated) = Nothing` stands.
  - Acquires across Translated channels resolve to the same window address.
  - Acquires on words written by passthrough channels reach the same physical memory: VRAM is coherent in L2, and sysmem is mapped with SNOOP on both sides.
- The fence, the NSI wake, and the `GP_GET` that kayfabe writes on the guest's behalf are unchanged.
- A refused address kills the channel by name before submission. No release lands and `GP_GET` does not advance (`hostile_entry_not_retired`), so a refusal is never a forged completion (A.3).
- **What changes for a buggy guest.** Suppose the guest unmaps a page behind in-flight work using the BAR0 invalidate path. Today the work faults. In the T-space it writes the old backing, which is still guest memory, because the address was bound earlier. That is legal stale-TLB behaviour, and the reach is unchanged.
- The completion probe logs both the guest VA and the rewritten window VA.

## 6. USERD and notifier bounds (`chan.rs:2741-2805`)

- **Passthrough framebuffer USERD:** require `base + USERD_SIZE (512) <= fb_len` before any host call. Today only 512-byte alignment is checked (`kf-host/src/channel.rs:535`, `:597`). This goes in `kf_chan::passthrough` as a pure constructor and is counted.
- **Sysmem USERD:** already bounded by `ram.file_range(base, 0x200)`.
- **Framebuffer error notifier:** require `off + 16 <= fb_len`. RM's ctxdma bound at `context_dma.c:510-514` remains as the second layer.
- **Translated framebuffer USERD:** the same bound. The CPU view is already bounded by RM (`mapping_cpu.c:369-371`); this check is defence in depth.

## 7. Alternatives rejected

- **A per-kernel-space T-space that keeps the guest kernel's mirror rows, plus a range bound on the ring and windows** (the check's recommendation 2+3). It is a denylist rather than a construction. It needs a T-space built and populated at the UVM flip, windows mapped per kernel space, and an extra method list for every address-bearing method. The monitored-fence, render-enable and `CLEAR_FAULTED` paths show that list is already incomplete.
- **Refusing virtual operands.** This breaks CeUtils and UVM (§1).
- **Mapping each sysmem operand on demand instead of a RAM window.** UVM migrates pageable memory 4 KiB at a time. That means a host map and unmap per page, held until the fence: hundreds of ioctls per 2 MiB block, plus mapping lifetime state.
- **Dropping the host twins of RM-internal (kernel-from-creation) spaces and keeping only their rows.** This would save their maps, but rows that no host map stands behind read as a "stored VA table" under §56 rule 2. Not proposed; the cost is small.

## 8. Cost

**Per operation.**
- One `BTreeMap` range lookup under a read lock per address trigger, sub-microsecond. That is about 2 per CeUtils push, 2-4 per UVM push, and 1 per PTE batch.
- Splits are rare (inline data crossing a page boundary) and are counted.

**Per Translated birth.** Two extra map and two extra unmap ioctls.

**Per mirror.** Two fewer window maps:
- store about 1 ms;
- RAM 65-86 ms at the bench's RAM size, scaling with guest RAM (§16.2).

The per-space page tables for a full guest-RAM mapping also go: derived, not measured, up to 2 MiB of host VRAM per GiB of guest RAM at 4 KiB PTEs, today paid in every live and spare mirror. Both `create_mirror` and `rpc_held` should drop.

**Per VM.** One T-space, about the cost of today's single prewarmed spare, off the vCPU, before the guest runs.

**Code.** Roughly +900 / -300 lines.

## 9. Rollout (each step pushed, CI green, box evidence committed)

0. **Independent hardening, today's tree.**
   - USERD and notifier bounds.
   - The current rewriter refuses `CLEAR_FAULTED`, `SET_MONITORED_FENCE_SIGNAL_ADDR_*`, `SET_RENDER_ENABLE_A/B` and the CC address methods by name.
1. **Build the T-space at prewarm, unused.** Log line `tspace space=… fb=…+… ram=…+… rings=…`. Measure the build cost.
2. **Rewriter T-mode and bind-at-submit** in `kf-chan`. Pure, with property tests.
3. **`KF3_TSPACE=1`, default off.** It moves Translated births to the T-space with sub-range ring maps, and the same knob removes windows and ring slots from mirrors. Update gates 3 and 4. A/B box runs.
4. **Default on.** Then delete the window, ring-slot and spare-window code and fold the doc corrections (§10). P1 closes here.
5. **With the G/K split (§N), move the T-space and rings to client K.**

This is a security-policy change, so it needs owner review before merge (§F).

## 10. Doc corrections (fold above the corrected text, dated)

- `THE_TRANSLATED_PLANE.md` §12, the window bullet: superseded. Windows live only in the per-VM T-space; UVM's mixed apertures are handled by rewriting virtual operands through the rows.
- §24.2's *"runs verbatim in a host VA space that mirrors the guest's kernel VA space"*: superseded the same way.
- New §28 "The T-space".
- `THE_CONSTRAINTS.md`: the §3 invariant, plus the rule *"a host VA space that runs guest-authored work maps only guest memory"*.
- The rewriter's module doc (`translated.rs:26`): corrected.

## 11. Unverified

- How long a full guest-RAM window takes to map at production RAM sizes. Only 8 GiB has been measured.
- That RM places both windows below 2^40 in a space with no guest reservations on every host driver in the matrix. Only GA106/580 has been measured.
- Whether GSP validates a host `CLEAR_FAULTED` handle.
- The DUP of the store and RAM object into K: allowed by the source, not measured.
- That stock CeUtils and UVM never push block-linear or discontiguous multi-line virtual operands, monitored fences or render-enable. The rollout's refusal counters measure this before default-on.

## 12. P0 interaction (one paragraph, P0's lane)

The ogkm-580 facts below were read for this design; their consequences for P0 are reasoned from the code, not measured.
- `rmclientIsAdmin` is false for a `NV01_ROOT_NON_PRIV` root (`client.c:88`, `:393`). But `escape.c:394-403` rewrites `NV01_ROOT`, `_CLIENT` and `_NON_PRIV` to `NV01_ROOT_CLIENT` for every userspace alloc, so kf3 can never set `bIsRootNonPriv`.
- What decides is `osIsAdministrator()` (`CAP_SYS_ADMIN`) of the thread issuing the channel alloc (`escape.c:304`, then `kernel_channel.c:276-290`).
- So "clear a bit" means dropping `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` from the effective set of the threads that birth channels, plus the reply bit-5 assert. No refusal is needed.

T channels are correct either way, because §3 guarantees no privileged operation reaches them.

owner_questions:
You said Translated should have "at most the single store guest vram mapped". The design keeps a guest-RAM window in the T-space alongside the store window, because:
- UVM migrations and CeUtils sysmem operands are guest-physical addresses;
- UVM's pushbuffer inline data and its tracking semaphores live in guest RAM by default.

What this means:
- Without a RAM window, each sysmem operand would need a host map and unmap held until its fence: hundreds of ioctls per 2 MiB migration.
- The reach is all of guest RAM. That is the same reach a guest kernel's physical-mode copy engine has on bare metal without an IOMMU, and it is never any VMM memory.
- It cannot be narrowed without modelling a vIOMMU.

Do you accept the guest-RAM window in the T-space, or do you want sysmem operands mapped per operand at that cost?

findings: The design is sound in direction, but it does not yet hold. I read it against kf-master origin/master 12a526df: crates/kf-* are unchanged since 784465a1, and the design's 7c9234d2 is one commit behind and docs-only. I also read ogkm-580 at /workspace/nvidia-gpu-passthrough/research_clones/ogkm-580.159.04. These claims hold: Translated work runs in C1's mirror, not in C2 or C3 (crates/kf-qemu/src/chan.rs:2945-2947). Both windows are mapped in every mirror (mem.rs:1755-1762). Today's rewriter forwards every host method below 0x100, including CLEAR_FAULTED 0x84, and every unclassified CE method verbatim (crates/kf-chan/src/translated.rs one_write: `if m < 0x100 { emit }` and `_ => {}` then emit). CeUtils completions are virtual (channel_utils.c:668-673, 733-746). Data operands are physical on every non-coherent family (uvm_gpu.h:1679-1692; ce_phys_vidmem_write_supported). The P0 mechanism is correct: kernel_channel.c:276-291 reads pCallContext->secInfo.privLevel, which is set on each ioctl from capable(CAP_SYS_ADMIN) (escape.c:304, os-interface.c:378-380, nv-linux.h:537). cachedPrivilege is not consulted there, and escape.c:394-403 rewrites NV01_ROOT_NON_PRIV, so no request bit can avoid it.

[HIGH, will break Hopper and Blackwell] The method allowlists cannot be generated from the class headers, and the completeness test cannot fail where it matters. The open headers are trimmed:
- src/common/sdk/nvidia/inc/class/clc8b5.h has no method defines for LINE_COUNT, PITCH_IN or SET_SRC_PHYS_MODE. clc9b5.h has 0 method defines and clcab5.h has 10.
- clc86f.h and clc96f.h list only SET_OBJECT, MEM_OP_A-D, SEM_* and WFI, with no SEMAPHOREA-D, NOP or NON_STALL_INTERRUPT.

CeUtils emits methods those headers do not list on every family. channelAddHostSema (channel_utils.c:718-746, called at :849 and :986) pushes NV906F_SEMAPHOREA-D on Hopper and Blackwell too; only the fast-scrub path uses C86F SEM_ADDR (:697-710). Its CE methods are NVB0B5-named.

Consequences:
- A header-generated allowlist refuses CeUtils' own PB-get release, so RmInitAdapter fails on Hopper and Blackwell.
- An inherited (C7B5/C56F) allowlist makes the hwref completeness test pass vacuously, for example on clc9b5.h. It then cannot catch an offset that a newer class reassigns to an address.

Fix: write per-family tables that state, per offset, which earlier class they inherit from. Gate them on a measured, count-only census of what stock CeUtils and UVM emit per family, and key the completeness test on that census. Classify by semantics, not by name. Cases the design does not list:
- LAUNCH_DMA SEMAPHORE_TYPE 3, CONDITIONAL_INTR (clc7b5.h);
- SET_MONITORED_FENCE_TYPE (0x21C), which arms a write to SIGNAL_ADDR state at launch;
- SET_RENDER_ENABLE_C (0x25C) alone, which selects a conditional mode against A/B state already in the engine;
- PM_TRIGGER (0x140).

[HIGH, a test that cannot fail] The headline property `every_emitted_address_is_a_window_address` decodes only the address pairs it already knows: OFFSET_*, SET_SEMAPHORE_A/B, SEMAPHOREA/B and SEM_ADDR_LO/HI. An address-bearing method that slips the allowlist passes it. Examples are MONITORED_FENCE_SIGNAL_ADDR, RENDER_ENABLE_A/B, the Hopper CC address methods (0x514-0x53C), and a Hopper SEMAPHOREA misclassified as address-free. Its negative control, today's rewriter forwarding virtual operands, does not show the test can see this class. Fix: also assert that every emitted (subchannel, method) is in the explicit allowlist or the rewritten-address set. Add a negative control that feeds SET_MONITORED_FENCE_SIGNAL_ADDR_* through today's rewriter and must fail. Separately, `a_guest_address_register_value_is_never_emitted` is vacuous whenever the result is a refusal, because nothing is emitted. Add a case where a row covers the VA, so a rewrite is emitted and its words are checked.

[MEDIUM-HIGH] P1's isolation claims depend on P0, and the proposed THE_CONSTRAINTS rule cannot be met as worded. The rule is 'a host VA space that runs guest-authored work maps only guest memory'. Host RM places its own privileged GR context buffers, including the global ones shared per gfid, in the host hole of every twin that has a GR channel (crates/kf-host/src/channel.rs:57-97; gfx7 measured FAULT_PRIV_VIOLATION when a guest ROP hit one). Only the PRIV PTE bit protects them, which holds only while twin channels are USER. Under CAP_SYS_ADMIN every passthrough twin channel is ADMIN, so removing the windows does not bound what such a channel can reach. Fix:
- Reword the rule to 'nothing kayfabe owns, and nothing but guest memory at user privilege'.
- Make the bit-5 birth-reply assert a stated precondition of every P1 claim.
- Have BOX T-WINDOW-USER and the regression A/B record bit 5 of each birth reply and CapEff, not only the build test.

P0 note: the bit-5 assert covers only kf-host births. libcuda's channels in C2 and C3 (cuCtxCreate on the VA and display threads) are ADMIN under the same capability and cannot be asserted from kf-host. The effective-set drop must reach those threads before cuInit, not only the birth workers.

[MEDIUM] The store window is not 'nothing kayfabe owns'. fb_layout (crates/kf-chip/src/bar0.rs) puts kayfabe's own declared BAR1 page directory and BAR2 root page inside the firmware carve-out: bar1_pde_base and bar2_pde_base are offsets from carve = fb_length - FW_CARVE_OUT_BYTES. map_window maps the whole store, and Windows::translate bounds LocalFb only by fb_len (chan.rs:493-499). Both today's physical arithmetic and the new virtual resolver can therefore write kayfabe-declared roots that the walker later reads. The guest publishes BAR2 PDE3[0] by RPC (fn 70), not by CE. Stock guest RM treats the carve-out as reserved and never targets it. So bounding T-space translation to [0, carve) costs no compatibility. Alternatively, name every consumer of those pages as treating them as guest-writable.

[MEDIUM, overstated claim plus an unmeasured assumption] Bind-at-submit is not the same as translation at execution time across channels. The §5 claim 'legal stale-TLB behaviour' covers only splits inside one channel. A piece pushed to the host ring behind a host acquire is bound before the releasing channel's walk or BAR0 invalidate completes; on bare metal it would translate after the acquire. Stock producers seem safe, because their virtual operands are static:
- UVM waits its kernel-mapping PTE writes (uvm_mmu.c uvm_page_table_range_vec_write_ptes_gpu ends in uvm_tracker_wait_deinit);
- CeUtils' pbGpuVA is fixed.

This is still unmeasured. Add a stale-bind counter: re-resolve each bound piece when its fence retires and count mismatches, with a fault-injected positive control. If that counter is ever non-zero, make a host acquire a bind barrier. Reach stays within guest memory either way, so this is a correctness and in-guest (A.9) concern, not an escape.

[LOW-MEDIUM] Remove the lazy T-space build ('built in prewarm and lazily if prewarm has not run'). That path pins the guest-RAM object inside the first Translated birth, which is CeUtils during RmInitAdapter, behind a held reply. Pinning took 299 ms at 8 GiB and scales with RAM, and the pr1 first mirror measured 7.6 s against the 6 s GSP RPC timeout (Xid 119). Refuse by name, or wait for prewarm, instead of building on that path.

[LOW] §6 bounds must use the declared USERD size, not 512. The Translated birth zeroes `declared` bytes taken from UserdMem::{Framebuffer,Sysmem}{size} (chan.rs ~2930-2937, kf_chan::host::zero_userd). Bound base + max(declared, USERD_SIZE) against fb_len or registered RAM.

[LOW] The zero-count box gates need a known positive in the same run. BOX T-UVM-FLIP's '0 refusals of every new name' and 'flip_suppressed=0' are silent zeros. The hostile checks that move those counters run in a different harness (kf-gate3/4). Exercise each new counter once per run with an injected negative control (KF3_NEGCTL_*) before trusting a zero.

[LOW, existing, outside the design but it will confuse the matrix] On Hopper and later, UVM writes SET_PB_SEGMENT_EXTENDED_BASE control GPFIFO entries (uvm_channel.c:2532-2543, uvm_hopper_host.c:419-425). kf_abi::submit::gp_entry_decode turns control entries into None and decodes only address bits 39:0. Hopper and Blackwell UVM pushbuffers sit above 2^40, so the Translated ring would read the wrong VA. A failure of T-UVM-FLIP or the regression A/B on those families would come from this, not from the T-space. Either scope the box matrix or fix it first.

[NOTED, not defects] The owner question about the guest-RAM window is justified as written: UVM's pageable-memory DMA mappings are invisible without a vIOMMU. The physical-RAM path refuses a second memfd rather than guessing (mem.rs:139-143). Window PTE attributes differ from the guest leaf's only in permissions: rows map uncompressed kinds already (ledger.rs Desired.kind), so carrying MapPerm is enough. Re-encoding every emitted method from decoded tuples also means a parser differential, such as legacy GRP2 forms decoded as incrementing, cannot bypass the emitted-method checks.
